Website design in Cleveland, Ohio has a particular customer in mind on this page: the plumber who knows how to work around cast iron stacks, the roofer who tears off three layers, the plasterer, the painter who handles lead-safe work, and the office manager at a small dental or therapy practice. Cleveland's homes are among the oldest in the country, and the people who keep them standing need a site that says plainly what they fix and where they go. Dominion Web Design Pro writes those sites by hand, shows you a free demo first, and charges once.

A city of old houses keeps a lot of trades busy

Cleveland had about 365,000 residents in the Census Bureau's 2024 estimate, living in a housing stock that predates most of the country's. In the American Community Survey for 2012 to 2016, 53.6% of the city's 211,387 housing units were built in 1939 or earlier. Across the wider Cleveland area, the median occupied home was built in 1959 in the 2011 American Housing Survey, against 1974 nationally.

Old houses mean steady work: boilers and radiators, galvanized pipe, slate and multi-layer roofs, sagging porches, knob-and-tube wiring, wood windows, tuckpointing on brick foundations. A homeowner with one of those problems searches for the specific job, not just "contractor." The site that names the job, with photos of that kind of work, gets the call.

Lead-safe rules created a line of work that customers search for

Cleveland requires owners of rental units built before 1978 to prove those units are lead safe. Owners submit a clearance exam or a lead risk assessment done by a private, state-approved professional, renew every two years through the Department of Building and Housing, and owner-occupied homes are exempt. Enforcement began March 31, 2021, phased in by ZIP code, with every rental unit due by March 31, 2023.

That rule sent a lot of landlords looking for help: assessors, painters and contractors who do lead hazard control, and the people who handle window and trim replacement. If you offer any of that, your site should say so in the landlord's own words, name the paperwork you can help with, and list the neighborhoods you cover. A page like that answers a search a general "home improvement" page never will.

  • A separate page for each service, from boiler repair to lead hazard control.
  • Photos of real jobs, and a short note on what was done.
  • A form that asks for the address, the year the house was built and the problem.
  • The neighborhoods and suburbs you drive to, named one by one.

Cleveland web development and web design, in plain words

A lot of Cleveland owners search for web development when what they need is web design, and the other way around. Here is the short version, so you know what to ask for.

What it makesThe pages customers see: words, layout, photos, buttons.The working parts: code, databases, logins, integrations.

Every site we build is still developed properly underneath: fast on a phone, with clean titles and descriptions, a sitemap submitted to Google, and schema markup on Pro and Agency. That part is simply not something you have to manage.

Clinics, practices and the businesses around the hospitals

Health care is the other big story in Cleveland's economy. In the state's December 2022 Ohio Major Employers Report, Cleveland Clinic topped the list with 56,986 Ohio employees, ahead of Walmart's 55,262. Around the big systems are many small, independent practices: dentists, physical therapists, chiropractors, counselors, home care agencies and medical billing offices.

Those practices compete for attention with hospital systems that have entire marketing departments. They will not out-spend them. What they can do is be clearer: who the provider is, which insurance they take, what a first visit looks like, where to park, and a phone number that is one tap away. Patients choosing between a big system and a small practice often decide on exactly those details.

Cleveland website design by neighborhood and suburb

Clevelanders talk about the East Side and the West Side first, and then the neighborhood. On the West Side, Ohio City grew up around the West Side Market at West 25th Street and Lorain Avenue, whose market hall opened in 1912 and today houses more than 70 vendors. Tremont sits just across the bridge from downtown, and Detroit Shoreway is home to the Gordon Square Arts District. Slavic Village, around Broadway, sits on the southeast side, and North Collinwood includes the Waterloo area on the East Side.

Beyond the city line are suburbs with their own searches: Lakewood, Parma, Euclid, Shaker Heights and more. A company based in Parma that works across Cuyahoga County should have a page for each place it actually serves, written about that place. That is how Cleveland website design for a service business turns into calls from the right ZIP codes.

Why a Cleveland website design has to answer local searches

Google says local results rest on relevance, distance and prominence. A homeowner in Tremont sees nearby companies first; that is distance. Reviews, links and mentions build prominence over time. Relevance is the part your website controls: how clearly it says which jobs you do and which neighborhoods you cover. Pro adds Google Business Profile setup and schema markup to help with that. We do not promise rankings, because nobody honestly can.

A Cleveland web designer who works from Texas

Straight answer on location: Dominion Web Design Pro has no office in Cleveland. Maurice Johnson builds every site from Big Sandy in East Texas and delivers it remotely, by link, phone and email.

For a contractor that changes less than it sounds: you send photos from the job, answer questions by phone, and approve pages from your truck. If you want someone across the desk every month, a local Cleveland web design agency will suit you better.

Common questions

How much does website design cost in Cleveland, Ohio?

It ranges from a few hundred dollars for a template to many thousands for an agency build with a retainer. Dominion Web Design Pro prints its prices: $497 for a 5-page Starter site, $997 for Pro and $1,997 for Agency, all one time. Hosting, maintenance and updates are included while you keep the AI agent, or $49 a month without it.

What is the difference between Cleveland web development and web design?

Web design is the site your customers see and read: the pages, the words, the layout, the photos, the call and contact buttons. Web development is the engineering underneath, and for bigger projects it means custom software such as patient portals, ordering systems or dashboards. A contractor or a private practice usually needs design done well on a solid, fast build, not custom software.

How do I choose a Cleveland web designer for a contracting business?

Ask for the price in dollars, who will own the site and domain, what a change costs later, and to see something built for your trade before you pay. Then look at it on your phone, because that is where homeowners will see it. A good Cleveland web designer, or a remote one, answers all four without hedging.

Can you build pages for Lakewood, Parma, Euclid and other suburbs?

Yes. The Pro package includes ten city pages, each researched and written separately, so a roofer who works Lakewood, Parma and Shaker Heights gets a real page for each. Agency starts with keyword research across your whole service area and builds a page for every town and service pair worth having, usually 30 to 60 pages.

Is Dominion a Cleveland web design company?

No. We are based in Big Sandy, East Texas, and we build remotely. You see the free demo and approve every page by link, and you can call (903) 636-7511 any hour; an AI receptionist answers and can transfer you to Maurice.
